record.body:
## Requirements

R1: Before selecting `planned` ready work, execute-phase selects `in_progress` work-items in the current phase whose latest assessment (structured) or latest check-run (simple) says retry (`next: execute` or `result: fail`), whose executor is not currently running, and re-dispatches each with the same executor mode.
R2: Each re-dispatch records a `project:assignment-amendment` whose `## Correction` quotes the failing check-run evidence (runner output tail) and the assessment's `## Reason` when present.
R3: Each re-dispatch increments optional work-item payload `attempts` (integer, default 0 when absent).
R4: When the phase's closing verification task fails and the cause is another task's code, the parent creates a new fix work-item in the same phase (Approach from the failure, acceptance = the failing check) with no `depends_on`, and adds a `depends_on` edge from the verification task to that fix item so `derived.ready` re-gates verification. `done` work-items are never transitioned back.
R5: A hard retry budget applies per task (default: 2 re-dispatches, or cumulative running time of 2× `estimate_minutes` when set, whichever comes first) and per phase for fix tasks (default: 3). Defaults are overridable in the phase body's run facts. The evidence ladder still routes; the budget only decides when to stop.
R6: When a budget is exhausted, the parent opens a blocking `project:continuity-question` (`scope: retry:<task-slug>`), a `project:finding` with `needs: human` summarizing attempts, and stops dispatching that task (dashboard Needs you).
R7: plan-phase consumes an assessment with `next: plan` by adding the missing task(s) for the uncovered requirement and re-opening plan review for the delta.
R8: The dashboard shows `attempt n/budget` on retried work-item rows.
R9: Skills (`execute-phase`, `verify-work`, `plan-phase`) and the contract stay consistent; focused tests cover re-dispatch selection, fix-task creation and re-gating, budget exhaustion, and no re-open of `done`.

## Acceptance criteria

- execute-phase re-selects and re-dispatches qualifying `in_progress` tasks and writes an assignment-amendment with failure evidence (tests for selection and amendment).
- A failing closing verification produces a fix work-item plus a new `depends_on` on the verification task; verification becomes ready again only after the fix is `done`; `done` items are never reopened.
- Exhausted per-task or per-phase budget creates a blocking continuity-question and `needs: human` finding and stops dispatch of that task.
- Budget defaults are documented; phase run facts can override them.
- plan-phase handles `next: plan` (skill text + focused test and/or skill↔contract consistency).
- Dashboard shows attempt/budget on retried rows (model/app test).
- `tests/test_skill_contract_consistency.py` stays green; contract declares optional `attempts` on work-item when used.

## Constraints

- Single-writer store: parent session writes records; executors and reviewers return evidence only.
- Binary `tdd`/`check` check-runs remain runner-authored (`check-run-authority`).
- Evidence escalation (`evidence-escalation` decision) is unchanged for routing level; budget is an orthogonal stop.
- Phase Landing / worktree rules from prior decisions stay in force.
- Tiered verification and the phase-end reviewer are out of scope; they will reuse this fix-task and budget mechanism later.

## Non-goals

- CI owning the full suite
- Per-task worktrees
- Replacing evidence escalation with a fixed failure count for level routing
- Changing dashboard dismiss / approval UX (#8)
- Implementing the phase-end reviewer or tiered verification

## Invariants

- `done` work-items are never transitioned back to `in_progress` or `planned`.
- Fix tasks are new work-items; they do not mutate completed siblings except via new `depends_on` edges on the verification task.
- Budget exhaustion always surfaces Needs you; it never silently continues dispatch.
- Re-dispatch preserves the wave's executor mode (`inline` or `subagent`).

## Assumptions

- Latest assessment / latest check-run for a task is well-defined from existing store queries.
- Closing verification is identifiable as the work-item that `depends_on` every other phase work-item (existing execute-phase convention).
- Runner output tails are available for amendments via the check runner (#5 / check-runner phase).
